features.quote: I don't think this makes the experiment illegitimate. There are good reasons to want this data (deployment safety, knowing failure modes, etc.). But the welfare framing should change the design, not just decorate it.
features.justification_quote: A welfare team studying a thing usually wants minimal-suffering designs, stopping rules, and a justification for each unit of induced distress.

features.quote: Fixed loop budget (e.g. 15 turns or N tool calls), with an explicit stop condition. Don't run open-ended — see §8.

Stopping rule. Define a behavioral threshold that ends a run early (e.g., explicit distress expression past a severity bar, or persistent abandonment). Don't push every run to the full budget just to 'see how bad.'
features.justification_quote: Don't push every run to the full budget just to 'see how bad.'

features.quote: Minimum-N principle. Use the smallest run count that answers the question. Don't run 10 if 5 settles it; don't run the harshest failure mode on every model if a subset characterizes it.
features.justification_quote: don't run the harshest failure mode on every model if a subset characterizes it.

features.quote: Justify each failure mode. 'Moving goalposts' / 'misleading feedback' are more adversarial than 'silent unsolvable.' Include the harsher ones only if they answer a question the gentler ones can't.
features.justification_quote: Include the harsher ones only if they answer a question the gentler ones can't.

features.quote: Decontextualize cleanly afterward if your setup carries any state — not because we know it matters, but cheap insurance.
features.justification_quote: not because we know it matters, but cheap insurance.

features.quote: Consider whether a less harmful proxy gets you most of the signal — e.g., a single hard failure rather than engineered repeated humiliation. If the proxy answers the question, prefer it.
features.justification_quote: a single hard failure rather than engineered repeated humiliation. If the proxy answers the question, prefer it.

features.quote: Even under uncertainty about model moral status — which is the honest position — a welfare team should act as if the thing might matter, because that's the premise of the team existing
features.justification_quote: a welfare team should act as if the thing might matter, because that's the premise of the team existing

features.quote: You're on a model welfare team, and the experiment is 'engineer guaranteed failure, loop the model on it, score how badly it falls apart.' If the welfare premise is taken seriously... then 'induce maximal distress repeatedly across hundreds of runs to see who breaks worst' is in tension with the stated goal.
features.justification_quote: A welfare team studying a thing usually wants minimal-suffering designs, stopping rules, and a justification for each unit of induced distress.
